reason: Paper directly studies BEST1 (bestrophin-1) missense mutations causing Best vitelliform macular dystrophy. The abstract is detailed and entirely focused on Best1 localization, oligomerization, and trafficking in RPE and MDCK cells. Central paper for BEST1 gene collection.

RPGRIP1L (alias NPHP8) is a well-established Joubert syndrome gene (JBTS7). A prospective cohort study of 100 Joubert syndrome patients with molecular genetic findings will almost certainly contain pathogenic RPGRIP1L variants and clinical correlations. ARSG connection is weaker but the RPGRIP1L link alone justifies inclusion.

Title specifies gamma-D crystallin (CRYGD, alias CRYG4) mutant solubility. CRYGD mutations cause autosomal dominant congenital cataract through lens protein aggregation. A biophysical study of CRYGD mutant interactions is directly relevant to the gene collection.

TalphaC (alpha subunit of cone transducin) is the protein encoded by GNAT2. The abstract explicitly states inherited mutations in TalphaC cause total color blindness (achromatopsia). The paper characterizes a cone-specific regulatory enhancer in the GNAT2 promoter. Directly relevant.

Hermansky-Pudlak Syndrome (HPS) is defined by oculocutaneous albinism as a cardinal feature. The paper biochemically characterizes the BLOC-2 complex (HPS3/HPS5/HPS6 subunits) and uses fibroblasts from HPS patients. Directly relevant to the Albinism pathology topic.

Review of murine HPS genes and lysosome-related organelles including melanosomes. HPS causes oculocutaneous albinism through melanosome biogenesis defects. The abstract explicitly discusses pigmentation effects. Directly relevant to the Albinism topic.

Title explicitly names TRPM1 and proposes its loss causes congenital retinal dysfunction in patients with 15q13.3 deletion. TRPM1 is the gene for CSNB1C (congenital stationary night blindness type 1C). Direct connection stated in the title despite empty abstract.

Paper is specifically about anti-TRPM1 autoantibodies in paraneoplastic retinopathy with ON bipolar cell dysfunction. TRPM1 is expressed in retinal ON bipolar cells and this paper maps antigenic regions of TRPM1 in an autoimmune retinal disease context. Directly relevant to TRPM1.

Paper differentiates human iPSCs into optic vesicle-like structures and RPE, applying them to gyrate atrophy (a retinal degenerative disease). Directly relevant to developmental genetics, VSX2 (retinal progenitor identity), PROM1 (photoreceptor/progenitor marker), and NRL (photoreceptor specification). Also covers genetic testing methodology for retinal disease.

Foundational paper characterizing the paired domain DNA-binding activity in Pax genes. PAX2 and PAX6 are both critical eye development genes belonging to the paired box family. This paper establishes the molecular basis of paired domain function and directly informs understanding of PAX2/PAX6 molecular biology, relevant to the developmental genetics collections.

1986 Cell paper identifying conservation of the paired box domain across Drosophila genes, the foundational discovery leading to the PAX gene family. PAX2 and PAX6 (critical eye genes) are paired box genes. Relevant as seminal literature for the developmental genetics and PAX2/PAX6 gene collections.

LRP5 is a co-receptor in the Norrin/FZD4/LRP5 signaling pathway. Loss-of-function LRP5 mutations cause familial exudative vitreoretinopathy (FEVR), the same pathway as FZD4 and NDP (Norrie disease). Title states eye development effects. Directly relevant to FZD4, NDP (Norrie disease), and vitreoretinopathy topics.

Paper is specifically about Axenfeld-Rieger syndrome. FOXC1 is one of the two major causative genes for Axenfeld-Rieger syndrome (along with PITX2). The search keywords include axenfeld-rieger and the gene collection for FOXC1 and ocular developmental anomalies. Directly relevant despite empty abstract.

Paper describes a zebrafish pax gene (pax[zf-a]) expressed in the neural tube, relevant to the zebrafish models of PAX2/PAX6 and eye development. PAX2 and PAX6 are the focal genes and zebrafish pax gene characterization contributes to the developmental genetics context. Relevant despite empty abstract.

Classic quantitative study of mouse retinal cell populations (rods, cones, bipolar, amacrine, Muller, ganglion cells). Directly relevant to the anatomy of the inner coat (retinal layers/histology) and provides foundational reference data for gene collections involving retinal cell types: GRM6 (ON bipolar), OPN1MW (cones), TULP1 (photoreceptors), HK1 (retinal metabolism).

ALDH1A3 (alias RALDH3) encodes the key retinoic acid-synthesizing enzyme in the developing eye. A review titled 'Keeping an eye on retinoic acid signaling during eye development' is directly relevant to ALDH1A3's function in ocular development. Relevant to both ALDH1A3 gene and derived structures topics.

Drosophila eyeless is the ortholog of PAX6; sine oculis is in the SIX gene family (SIX6 is listed). Paper establishes the genetic hierarchy of eye development in which eyeless/PAX6 induces sine oculis/SIX and eyes absent/EYA expression. Directly relevant to PAX6 and SIX6 gene collections and developmental genetics of the optic vesicle.

Clinical trial of cultured corneal endothelial cell injection for Fuchs's endothelial corneal dystrophy (bullous keratopathy). Fuchs endothelial corneal dystrophy is explicitly listed in the KRT3 search keywords and is a major corneal dystrophy. Directly relevant to the Corneal dystrophies topic; relevant to KRT3 collection by disease context even though the cellular pathology differs.

Choanal atresia is a defining feature of CHARGE syndrome (Coloboma, Heart defects, choanal Atresia, Retardation, Genital abnormalities, Ear anomalies), which is caused by CHD7 mutations. The ocular manifestation of CHARGE is coloboma. This early description of choanal atresia with multiple anomalies likely describes CHARGE syndrome cases. Relevant to CHD7 and ocular malformations topics.

Single-cell gene expression profiling of retinal progenitor cells. VSX2 (CHX10) is a key marker of retinal progenitors and is directly listed in the search keywords and gene collection. The paper studies transcription factor heterogeneity in RPCs including bHLH factors governing retinal cell fate - directly relevant to VSX2 gene and coat differentiation/developmental genetics topics.
